summary: Backend-only regression + new-features test for iteration 2 (watchlist, alerts, RTSP cameras, settings, kiosk). 63/63 pytest cases passed on first clean run (30 original + 33 new). Verified real end-to-end paths: watchlist transitions on an enrolled portrait, /api/recognize/multi returning watchlist_status='vip'/'blocked' AND creating matching alert rows, noise-frame path creating unknown alert with image_url + best-similarity, /api/alerts list is timestamp-desc with since filter, /api/alerts/{id}/read + read-all persist correctly and require auth, /api/cameras full CRUD with fake RTSP URL correctly transitioning to state='error' (CameraWorker logs 'cannot open rtsp://…'), /api/cameras/{id}/status returns state='stopped' for unknown/deleted cameras, /api/settings requires auth and round-trips alert_email + kiosk_token, /api/settings/test-email admin-only endpoint returns 502 (Resend sandbox rejects example.com addresses) — endpoint contract validated, /api/kiosk/verify is public (no Bearer) but requires kiosk_token (401 on wrong token, known/unknown/no_face on real portrait/noise frames), dashboard stats now includes cameras_total + cameras_online + unread_alerts. Regression: all previously passing endpoints from iteration_1 (auth, users CRUD, enroll, recognize single & multi, attendance, recognition-history, unknowns, dashboard) still pass.

minor.issue: Returns 502 with Resend sandbox key because SENDER_EMAIL=onboarding@resend.dev + example.com recipient is rejected ('Invalid `to` field'). Endpoint contract is correct; not a bug — user must configure the Resend-account-owner email as alert_email in production.
Idempotent but returns only {ok:true} — no count of rows updated. Nice-to-have to expose 'updated' count for frontend UX (e.g. toast 'Marked 12 alerts read').

When status=='unknown', response returns unknown_id but does not include the image_url; frontend has to derive it from /uploads/unknowns/{unk_id}.jpg. Consider returning image_url directly for consistency with the alert doc.
Silently ignores unknown fields — only name/url/enabled are accepted. If 'type' is sent, it's dropped without a 400. Minor DX issue.
Does not delete the user's thumbnail file /uploads/users/{id}.jpg from disk (only DB rows). Orphan files accumulate. Same for camera snapshots on DELETE /api/cameras/{id}.

Populates status via camera_manager.status(id) which returns {'state':'stopped'} for disabled cameras. Works correctly, but for enabled cameras whose worker had a fatal error, the 'error' string is stringified even when null — acceptable, just noting.

action_items: For production Resend delivery, either upgrade the Resend account (verify a domain) or set SENDER_EMAIL + alert_email to the Resend account-owner email so /api/settings/test-email returns 200.
Consider stripping orphan files on DELETE /api/users/{id} and DELETE /api/cameras/{id} (thumbnails + camera snapshots).
Optional: return {ok:true, updated:N} from /api/alerts/read-all so the UI can toast the affected count.
critical_code_review_comments: cameras.py CameraWorker._run runs cv2.VideoCapture(self.url) in a thread executor but there's no read-timeout wrapper — an unreachable RTSP that hangs opening can keep 'starting' for a long time. Consider `cv2.CAP_PROP_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MSEC` + `cv2.CAP_PROP_READ_TIMEOUT_MSEC` on FFmpeg backend, or a wall-clock guard.

cameras.py: worker publishes raw embedding lists inside status['last_detections'] which are then held in memory + passed to on_detections. Each 512-d vector = 2 KB; for a 5-camera fleet the manager keeps ~10 KB * detections in a hot dict. Not a bug, just watch it.

server.py: _on_camera_detections logs recognition_logs for EVERY per-second detection without any per-user cooldown. On a busy camera the recognition_logs collection will grow very fast. Consider a per (user_id, camera_id) debounce (e.g. skip if last log within N seconds) — mirrors what _log_attendance_if_needed already does for attendance.

server.py: KIOSK_UNKNOWN_ALERT_COOLDOWN_S is only applied to the RTSP-camera unknown path, not to POST /api/recognize/multi and /api/kiosk/verify — those two create an 'unknown' alert on every hit. Add the same cooldown to the manual endpoints to avoid alert-spam if the frontend polls repeatedly with the same noise frames.

server.py: POST /api/settings PATCH allows role='admin' only but the equivalent POST/PATCH for other admin-only settings paths (e.g. test-email) also gates on 'admin'. GET /api/settings on the other hand accepts any authenticated admin/operator — kiosk_token is effectively secret so consider gating GET behind 'admin' too, otherwise an operator can read the token and use the public kiosk endpoint.

alerts.py create_alert: on Resend failure (email_id=None) the alert is still stored in DB but there's no retry queue or delivery-failure flag. If Resend is misconfigured you silently lose email delivery — consider recording the failure reason on the alert doc.

server.py TestWatchlistAndAlerts triggers recognize/multi → the /api/recognize/multi path creates an unknown alert with best_frame_b64 even when status IS 'no_face'? Actually looking again: only when votes is non-empty AND top vote loses. On pure-noise images, votes==[] → returns 'no_face' immediately, no alert. So the 'unknown' alert path only fires when at least one detection was made but similarity < 0.42 — this is correct but subtle; consider adding an inline comment.
Deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event startup/shutdown hooks (same as iteration_1) — migrate to lifespan handlers.

The class-scoped pytest fixtures in test_new_features.py trigger PytestRemovedIn10Warning ('Class-scoped fixture defined as instance method'). Non-blocking but should switch to @classmethod / module-level in a future clean-up.
seed_data_creation: TestWatchlistAndAlerts creates a transient TEST_WATCH_Obama user, enrolls 4 real InsightFace embeddings from /app/test_fixtures/portrait.jpg, exercises watchlist transitions (normal→vip→blocked→normal), then deletes it in fixture teardown. TestCameras creates + deletes a TEST_CAM_lobby camera. TestSettingsAndKiosk sets kiosk_token='TEST_KIOSK_TOKEN_abc123' and alert_email='demo@example.com' in the settings collection (these persist in Mongo after the run — future test runs should reset or ignore).
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_new_features.py + test_face_recognition.py both run under pytest-xdist -n 2 --dist loadscope. loadscope groups by CLASS, so keep interdependent flows inside a single class. TestWatchlistAndAlerts and TestUserLifecycle both enroll the same obama.jpg portrait under two different user names — because the classes run on separate workers concurrently, the gallery briefly has TWO matching identities. The recognize/multi cosine matcher happens to pick the correct one in this run (thanks to identical L2-normalised embeddings + Mongo insertion order stability), but if you ever add a THIRD enrollee with the same portrait you'll get non-deterministic matches. Fix if it flakes: change one class to use a different portrait fixture or serialise the two classes onto one worker. Resend sandbox constraint: /api/settings/test-email currently returns 502 for demo@example.com — this is EXPECTED and the test asserts either 200 or 502 (only fails on 5xx crash or 401/403).
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no bugs to root-cause this iteration. All 4 new feature groups behaved as specified. The only surprise was Resend rejecting example.com recipients ('Invalid `to` field'), which produces the 502 documented in the task brief and is treated as expected endpoint-contract behaviour.
